topic: Assigning Salary Template (Contract) to an Employee
summary: This process allows you to assign a salary structure or contract to an employee, defining their earnings and deductions for a specified period. This is a foundational step before processing monthly salaries.
steps: Search for the desired employee by their ID or Name.
Select the employee using the checkbox.
Click the 'Assign Template' button at the bottom of the screen.
If the employee has a previous contract, you will see options like 'Copy from Salary Template'. If no previous contract, you will proceed to define a new one.
Choose a standard template (e.g., 'With PF, ESI both' or 'Without PF') or copy from an existing one.
Enter the 'Basic' amount. If applicable, also enter 'DA' or 'Grade Pay'.
Review the automatically calculated ESI and PF amounts. You can override these by setting them as 'Fixed' values if required (e.g., setting ESI to 101 and PF to 1612).
Add any additional deduction heads (e.g., 'Labour Welfare Fund' with a fixed amount like 27) or remove unnecessary employer contributions.
Click 'Calculate' to see the gross salary, total deductions, and paid salary based on the entered heads and amounts.
Set the 'End Date' for the contract. The 'Start Date' will typically be frozen based on the employee's joining date or the end date of a previous contract.
Click 'Assign' to finalize the contract assignment.
business_rules: If an employee already has an assigned contract, any new contract's start date must be after the end date of the previous contract.
Standard salary templates (e.g., With PF, Without PF, Without ESI PF) are available for quick selection.
ESI is typically calculated at 0.75% of basic salary, and PF at 12% of basic salary, but these can be set as fixed amounts.
The 'Up to amount' for ESI/PF indicates the maximum limit; the system calculates based on percentage first and caps at this limit if exceeded.
important_notes: Ensure you have complete HRM permissions to access and perform this action.
If you need to create a contract for a past month (e.g., November when a December contract is already assigned), the existing future contract must be removed first.
Changes made during contract assignment apply for the entire duration of the contract. Month-specific adjustments (like advance recovery) are typically handled during salary processing.
The system automatically calculates ESI and PF based on percentages unless you explicitly set them as 'Fixed' amounts.
